kilauea_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY DAILY UPDATE
kilauea_notices.message: HVO Kilauea ORANGE/WATCH - Eruption of intermittent precursory overflows from both the north and southwest Halemaʻumaʻu vents began at 1:21 a.m. on November 22. The modeled forecast for the onset of episode 57 fountaining is November 22-26.
kilauea_notices.detail: Overview: Continuous glow and spattering occurred overnight with precursory overflows starting from the north vent at 1:21 a.m. on November 22. The north vent has since had 3 overflows and the southwest vent has had 2 overflows that have reached several hundred yards from the vents. Summit tilt continues to show slow, stepwise inflation over the past 24 hours. Another fountaining episode remains likely and the current forecast window for episode 57 fountaining is November 22-26. A VAN/VONA raising the alert level from YELLOW/ADVISORY to ORANGE/WATCH was been issued in response to the start of precursory overflow activity from the north and southwest vents: https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/hans-public/notice/DOI-USGS-HVO-2026-11-22T13:52:55+00:00 Summit Observations: Intermittent, precursory overflows started from the north vent within Halemaʻumaʻu at approximately 1:21 a.m. HST on November 22, followed by north vent overflows at 2:06 am and 2:48 a.m., the last of which ended at 3:03 a.m. HST. Each north vent overflow lasted 15-20 minutes with the lava using multiple flow paths to reaching up to 500 yards from the vent. The southwest vent had overflows at approximately 5:08 a.m. and 5:20 a.m. HST, each of which lasted about 5 minutes with the lava making it hundreds of yards from the vent. Summit webcams recorded continuous strong glow and frequent spattering from both the north and southwest vents overnight. There have been several other occasions during which lava has been observed high in the vents that have not resulted in overflows. Intermittent overflows are expected to continue until the onset of episode 57 fountaining forecast for today through November 26. Seismic tremor remained continuous over the past day. Two earthquakes were located beneath the summit in the past day. The Uēkahuna tiltmeter (UWD) has recorded stepwise summit inflation since the end of episode 56 lava fountaining. The stepwise inflation recorded on tiltmeters across the summit consists of slow steady inflation separated by brief, 2-12 hour, steps with little or no inflation. As of this morning UWD had regained about 0.9 microradians of tilt during the past day, resulting in a total of about 15.6 microradians of inflationary tilt since the end of episode 56. The average sulfur dioxide (SO2) emission rate could not be accurately measured yesterday, November 21, due to dynamic wind conditions but is presumed to be between 2000 and 3000 metric tonnes of SO2 per day based on previous measurements. Trade winds this morning are carrying volcanic gases to the southwest. The National Weather Surface (NWS) forecasts surface winds at Kīlauea's summit will change from north-northeasterly trade winds to still conditions with a possibility of winds from the southwest beginning on Tuesday evening to Wednesday morning. Rift Zone Observations: Rates of seismicity and ground deformation remain low in the East Rift Zone and Southwest Rift Zone. SO2 emissions from the East Rift Zone remain below the detection limit. Analysis: Following the end of episode 56 on November 5, 2026, summit tiltmeters have recorded a typical post-fountaining recovery, with nearly continuous inflationary tilt at UWD. Tiltmeters showed inflationary tilt being recorded on the UWD tiltmeter over the past 24 hours, with periods of little or no inflation alternating in a stepwise fashion with slow, consistent inflation. flattening of the tilt at times. Modelling based on ongoing tilt trends, along with the onset of overflows, glow and minor spatter seen within the eruptive vents, all indicate another fountaining episode is likely. The modeled forecast window for episode 57 fountaining is November 22-26 with Monday November 23 to Wednesday November 25 being most likely. Changes from inflation to deflation at the summit can result in the dates of the forecast window being extended. mauna_loa_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY MONTHLY UPDATE
mauna_loa_notices.message: HVO Mauna Loa GREEN/NORMAL - Mauna Loa earthquake counts were within typical levels in October, and minor inflation continues.
mauna_loa_notices.detail: Mauna Loa had a slight increase in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 66 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the October reporting period, after 53 in September. These variations are within the typical range for the past two years. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks. Data from Global Positioning System (GPS) instruments on Mauna Loa showed slight inflation across the summit region in the past month. Oscillations between contraction and inflation patterns during non-eruptive periods are normal, but inflation has been the dominant trend since the 2022 eruption, consistent with magma refilling the summit reservoir system. Gas and temperature data from a station on Mauna Loa's Southwest Rift Zone indicate these values are at background levels, with little change relative to previous months. HVO continues to closely monitor Mauna Loa and will issue another update in one month, or earlier, should conditions change significantly.
